name: Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasm

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence reported in Caucasian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of neuroendocrine differentiation with immunohistochemical markers (chromogranin A, synaptophysin)
Tumor grading based on mitotic count and Ki-67 proliferation index
Radiological evidence of tumor localization and extent via CT, MRI, or somatostatin receptor scintigraphy/PET
Elevated serum markers such as chromogranin A and specific hormone levels depending on functional status

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with immunohistochemical markers plus tumor grading is required for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Functional tumors may require additional biochemical testing for hormone secretion profiles.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Flushing episodes due to carcinoid syndrome
Secretory diarrhea associated with hormone secretion
pathognomonic.notes: Common in functional tumors producing serotonin or vasoactive intestinal peptide

common.notes: Often nonspecific and related to tumor mass effect

searchTerms: unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

common.notes: May occur with tumors obstructing bile ducts
searchTerms: jaundice caused by bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellowing due to blocked bile
valve lesions in carcinoid heart disease

occasional.notes: Seen in VIPomas causing secretory diarrhea

occasional.symptomName: Peptic ulcer disease secondary to gastrin secretion

occasional.notes: May be related to hormone secretion

rare.symptomName: Cushingoid features due to ectopic ACTH secretion
searchTerms: symptoms of high cortisol due to ectopic hormone
signs of cortisol excess from tumor hormone

rare.symptomName: Hypotension related to vasoactive hormone secretion
searchTerms: blood pressure drops from tumor secretions

laboratory: Increased specific hormone levels (e.g., serotonin, gastrin, insulin, VIP)
Elevated 5-HIAA in 24-hour urine for serotonin-secreting tumors
imaging: CT or MRI showing primary tumor and metastases
Somatostatin receptor scintigraphy (Octreoscan) or PET with Ga-68 DOTATATE
genetic: Mutations in MEN1 gene in familial cases
Alterations in DAXX, ATRX, and mTOR pathway genes in sporadic tumors
other: Histopathology with immunohistochemistry positive for synaptophysin and chromogranin A
Ki-67 proliferation index for tumor grading

distinguishingFeatures: Lacks neuroendocrine markers chromogranin A and synaptophysin
Typically presents with more aggressive local invasion
Different imaging characteristics and tumor markers (e.g., CA 19-9 elevated)
Positive for c-KIT (CD117) and DOG1 immunostaining
Different histological appearance (spindle or epithelioid cells)

redFlags: Rapid onset of carcinoid crisis with flushing, bronchospasm, and hypotension
Unexplained hypoglycemia episodes in non-diabetic patients
New onset heart murmurs suggestive of carcinoid heart disease
references: WHO Classification of Tumours of the Digestive System, 5th Edition, 2019
Orphanet Report on Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms, ORPHA:100092
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Neuroendocrine Tumors, 2024
